newsitem.title: CHINA: Supervision a 1997 priority for Shanghai bourse.
newsitem.headline: Supervision a 1997 priority for Shanghai bourse.

text.p: The development of a stable and regulated market is a major priority of the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 1997, the Shanghai Securities News said on Monday.
The exchange will update its computer and satellite systems, and adjust its trading means and clearance system to enlarge market capacity, the newspaper said.

"The exchange will focus on the establishment of infrastructure and supervision so the market can develop with stability and regulation," Yang Xianghai, head of the exchange, was quoted by the newspaper as saying.
The exchange also planned to promote the foreign currency B share market and the state debt market, it said, but did not elaborate.
China's stock markets in Shanghai and the southern boomtown of Shenzhen, since opening in the early 1990s, have been marked by speculation and a lack of regulation.
China's regulatory authorities have been at pains to stress stable development and tighter regulation of the markets as they mature.
